pr_title: drivers: sensors: silabs: add gecko acmp
pr_body:
- Update module/hal_silabs to include acmp related files from HAL
- Update soc to include acmp related files if ACMP is required
- Add ACMP sensor driver
- Add ACMP nodes support for EFR32MG24 devices
- Add sample for ACMP sensor driver

Fixes #83529
pr_comments:
Hello @Martinhoff-maker, thank you for reviewing and good questions.

1) I hesitate to use comparator API but the lack of configuration on runtime (set/get attributes for example) for future integration led me to choose the sensor API.
Obviously: 
- Do we need attribute changes on runtime, even in the future for a comparator?
- Do we need counters or custom values integrations?
- Maybe the comparator API could be improved to integrate attributes like functions directly?
If you think comparator API is still the way to go: please let me know and I will update this PR
2) Let's go for clock_control() functions usage :)

> I hesitate to use comparator API but the lack of configuration on runtime (set/get attributes for example) for future integration led me to choose the sensor API.

I believe both option can be accepted. The API described in `doc/hardware/peripherals/comparator.rst` really match with ACMP. However, sensor framework seems more versatile.
@RomainPelletant FYI, another contributor also contacted me because he started a driver for ACMP. His implementation is rather different because it is based on the comparator framework.
@jerome-pouiller if someone else has a better proposal I won't force anything: please let me know and I will give up on this PR
@RomainPelletant, @silabs-chgalant has shared an early version of his work here:  https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/83980. Your feedback would be valuable.

Superseded by #83980.

@RomainPelletant, sorry for the duplicated work.
@jerome-pouiller no time to work on that now so glad to see the support for ACMP upstreamed :)

issue_context.title: gecko: add ACMP sensor driver support
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Analog comparator (ACMP) support for SiLabs gecko devices.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add driver support for ACMP

review_comments: It's a fairly new convention but I believe this should be using DEVICE_API().
hmm... I believe `val` is not defined.

The declaration of `GECKO_ACMP_CONFIG_FUNC_INIT()` 4 lines above has a parameter. Align this line with this previous declaration. (then, both declaration of `GECKO_ACMP_INIT_CONFIG()` will be identical)
`GECKO_ACMP_INIT_CONFIG()` seems useless. Instead, you can inline the declaration of `gecko_acmp_config_##n`.

Zephyr prefers to use the Zephyr API to manage clocks (`clock_enable()`). This API only exist on Series-2. However, since Series-0/1 is deprecated and it seems you mainly target xg24, I suggest to use `clock_enable()` and drop support for Series-1.

Once you only support Series-2, it will probably not make sense anymore to call this driver "gecko" ("gecko" is for Series 0/1 only). Probably `"silabs,acmp"` will be better.
This macro seem to conflict with `DT_INST_IRQN(n)`.
As for the clock, I suggest to use Zephyr API for IRQ management.
You can call `GECKO_ACMP_INIT_CONFIG()` before `SENSOR_DEVICE_DT_INST_DEFINE()` and get rid of this line.
Avoid to repeat the condition after `#endif` if the condition is obvious (because of the Don't Repeat Yourself rule).

I suggest to keep definitions of `SENSOR_CHAN_GECKO_ACMP_*_EDGE_COUNTER` even if `CONFIG_GECKO_ACMP_EDGE_COUNTER`. Thus, the caller code will simpler (it will be probably able to remove some a #ifdef, or at least to change them is `IS_ENABLE()`).

BTW, I wonder if it make sense to make all these features optional. This leads to increased maintenance cost. It make sense to make a feature optional if you could get rid of a dependency.
